documents.shelfmark: State Archives of Modena, Carteggio Principi Esteri, 1623, b. 2/2, 2, 18

plaintext.source: MDE III (1877), no. 75, pp. 93-96; manuscript decipherment slips in images P1/P4

transcription.source: MDE III (1877), no. 75, pp. 93-96; manuscript decipherment slips in images P1/P4
transcription.notes: 14 Nov 2026: the cipher passages (13 lines on page 1, three short lines on page 3) transcribed sign by sign from the public Vestigia 1976 photographs into transcr/R1143_transcription.txt, 445 signs (measured on the sign labels, without the word-break bars, dots, blots and clear words); a single AI transcription, not checked by a person, 3 signs marked doubtful. Before that: identified older reading by manuscript/edition comparison; no fresh exhaustive glyph transcript. R1143 photographs include repeated views with slips moved.

system.summary: A graphic substitution alphabet for passages inside a clear Italian letter of May 1486, with contemporary decipherment slips; not reconstructed here.
system.notes: Two months after R1142 (beatrice1486) announced a new cipher, so this letter may be in the new one; not established, and not grouped with it.

prior_solution.where: MDE III (1877), no. 75, pp. 93-96; contemporary decipherment slips photographed with the leaves (images P1, P4)

conditions.human_role: Supplied target catalogue entry and pointed out available DECODE cookie.

solution.what: Extracted five exact dates, recipients and shelfmarks from cached DECODE metadata; web reader could not open live DECODE page.
Used existing user-authorized DECODE cookie to acquire all 18 images. R1143 has repeated photographs with decipherment slips moved.
Located MDE III nos. 10 and 12 for both 1482 letters, III no. 75 for May 1486, IV supplement no. 45 for March cipher and III no. 54 for its closing.

Matched dates, clear wording, cipher boundaries and R1143 manuscript slips to older readings. Rendered print confirms italics and March Virtus/Fortis/M. markers. No exhaustive key verification claimed.
Entry split from beatrice1482 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R1143 is two months after R1142, which encloses a new cipher; the two are not shown to share a key.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the OCR extract of MDE III (1877) no. 75 as decryption; the contemporary slips exist only on the DECODE images (not transcribed) and no glyph transcription of the cipher exists (project work).

Looked for a transcription of the cipher: none in the folder, none on DECODE R1143 (six images only; full-size DECODE images need a login). Found the letter in the open Vestigia database as document 1976 (ASMo CPE b. 1623, 2, fasc. 1, no. 18), six public photographs.

Transcribed the cipher passages sign by sign from the Vestigia photographs with shape labels (transcr/R1143_transcription.txt): 13 lines on page 1 and three short lines on page 3, 445 signs, 41 distinct labels. By Claude (session of 14 Nov 2026), not checked by a person.

Checked the transcription by decoding: one value per sign, taken from the printed reading (MDE III no. 75) and the two slips, reproduces the whole passage as Italian (che ... vostro figliolo sia tanto amato ... se conferisca qua; lo prefato Andriolo). Not agreeing: 'aaate' where the print has Abbate (one sign doubtful), the sign L in 'su[L]icare' and '[L]illo' (print supplicare, slip quello), and the cipher writes esso, dali, el contrario where the print has epso, dalo, il contrario. Figures 16, 19, 21 and G 2, G 7 stand for names and a link word; x4 and n carry no letter. No key file written: the values come from the existing reading.

outcome.method_basis: The letter carries contemporary decipherment slips laid over the cipher, and MDE III (1877) no. 75 prints the reading; slips and print were matched to the DECODE images and no key was applied.
outcome.notes: Milanese support for Ippolito against Cardinal Ascanio's envoy; Andriolo to come. Six photographs show three written pages, two of them twice with the slips moved. Split on 14 Oct 2026 from beatrice1482.

texts.label: Buda, 2 May 1486
texts.summary: Beatrice of Aragon to her sister Eleonora of Ferrara: the Duke of Milan and the Duke of Bari support Ippolito d'Este, against the account of Cardinal Ascanio's envoy, the abbot of Forlì, and Andriolo is asked to come to Hungary. Contemporary decipherment slips are photographed over the cipher; the decryption here is the uncorrected OCR of the reading printed in MDE III (1877) no. 75.
